Conform Ducky code to SE-EDU Java coding standard
commitResults.messageBody:
The Ducky and chore classes break several rules of the SE-EDU Java
coding standard: the class name is lower-case, many braces and
operators lack surrounding spaces, two lines exceed the length
limit, and the public types and methods have no Javadoc. Two
compiled .class files are tracked by mistake as well.

Let's bring the Java tree in line with the standard:

- Rename class chore to Chore (PascalCase) and rename the file to
  match; update every reference in Ducky.
- Add a space before opening braces and around binary operators,
  and drop the space between a method name and its parenthesis.
- Wrap the two over-long println statements before the + operator.
- Replace the bare array size 100 with a named constant MAX_CHORES.
- Add class and method Javadoc, and correct a stale comment that
  referred to a "bye" command and to echoing input.
- Stop tracking Ducky.class and chore.class, and ignore *.class.

No behaviour change: command output is identical and the code
compiles on Java 25.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add mandatory SE-EDU Java coding standard skill
commitResults.messageBody:
The project has no written Java style rules, so naming, formatting,
and documentation have drifted across the code base.

Let's adopt the SE-EDU Java coding standard (Basic + Intermediate):

- Add the seedu-java-coding-standard skill, which captures the rules
  for naming, layout, statements, and Javadoc plus a pre-commit
  checklist.
- Require the skill from a new mandatory section in AGENTS.md so it
  is applied to all Java work, new and existing.
- Override one rule by project decision: comments and Javadoc use
  British spelling, not the American spelling the standard specifies.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Add mandatory SE-EDU Git conventions skill
commitResults.messageBody:
Commit messages in this repository are inconsistent and follow no
agreed format, which makes the history hard to read.

Let's adopt the SE-EDU Git conventions:

- Add the seedu-git-standard skill, covering commit-message format,
  commit granularity, branch naming, and tags.
- Require the skill from the Git section of AGENTS.md so it applies
  to all future commits and branches.
